Load interview data from a creel connection

Source: R/fetch-loaders.R
fetch_interviews.Rd

Reads the interviews table from a creel data source, renames columns to canonical tidycreel names, coerces types, validates, and returns a data frame ready for tidycreel::add_interviews().

Usage

fetch_interviews(conn, ...)

Arguments

conn

A creel_connection object created by creel_connect().

...

Reserved for future arguments.

Value

A data frame with canonical columns: interview_uid, date (Date), catch_count (numeric), effort (numeric), trip_status (character).

Six further columns are carried when the schema (CSV) or api_field_map (API) maps them, and omitted otherwise: n_anglers (numeric), angler_type (character), site (character), circuit (character), n_counted (numeric), n_interviewed (numeric). Map n_anglers whenever the source records party size – without it tidycreel::add_interviews() assumes one angler per interview and party-hours are consumed as angler-hours. site and circuit are what a bus-route design joins the site inclusion probability on.

Four more are carried on the same terms for the tidycreel summaries: angler_method (character), species_sought (character), refused (logical) and zip_code (character). refused accepts TRUE/FALSE, T/F, yes/no, Y/N and 1/0 in any case, and aborts on any other code rather than reading it as NA; pass it to tidycreel::add_interviews() so a refused interview is not taken for a no-catch party. zip_code is written as text, with a whole number padded back to five digits. angler_method and species_sought are carried as the source codes them: value_maps does not cover them, because tidycreel has no canonical vocabulary for either. On CSV and SQL, tidycreel::creel_schema() has no zip_code_col, so zip_code is carried only from a source column already named zip_code.

Source columns outside the map are dropped, and each fetch reports which ones by name.

On the API backend every row also carries creel_uid (character), the creel UID it was fetched for, so a connection to several creels returns them labelled rather than pooled.

When the API returns no rows, the result has no stratum columns. A fetch with rows carries each stratum in the source's own type, which an empty response does not reveal, and no zero-length guess binds with every type in dplyr::bind_rows(). Check for the column, or for nrow() == 0, before selecting a stratum.
